why: Brief 101, 'The square's camera: Sky picks B, the lamp mast' (Aster's step 5; Vantage's briefs/101/vantage/square-camera.md section 3 B). The terrace's west lamp beside the cell's start becomes the square's mast: the sphere lamp and the café's banner at lamp height, a chrome column to a crown at about 8 m, three camera pods fanned 60° over the café's side and front, the terrace and the square, their backs to the cell. The old words said 'On a mast over the square' and 'It turns between three views'. The engine sees through every head at once (sim Game.cs InHeads), and a loop, a cut or a shot darkens the whole camera (CameraWatching, CameraDark). The ids stay: camera-mast-z0 (the sim's mast-z0). Brief 102's bar: plain words, no rule explained.

edits.before: On a mast over the square. A person watches it live.
edits.after: On the lamp post by the café terrace. A person watches it live.
edits.why: Where it stands, in words anyone can see from the start: the terrace's west lamp, outside the terrace wall's west end. Like the other cameras' told lines ('On a pole by the public door.'), it names no view: what the lenses see is the Watch's to teach.

edits.before: Its cone covers the square. It turns between three views.
edits.after: Its three lenses watch at once: the café, the terrace and the square.
edits.why: Three fixed heads, all live together (InHeads), so it never turns. The heads, by the check below: N along the café's west side, ENE over its front and the terrace, ESE over the square and the fountain. 69 characters (≤ 70 after 'Learned: ').

edits.before: Watch it from close by to learn what it sees. Needs a clear line.
edits.after: Watch it from close by to learn what its three lenses see. Needs a clear line.
edits.why: The tip names the three lenses the Watch will show.

edits.before: Study the lens: its cone, and when it turns. Needs a clear line.
edits.after: Study the three lenses: their cones, their blind side. Needs a clear line.
edits.why: 'when it turns' was untrue. Its blind side is behind it, at the kerb where the cell starts; the pickup camera's tip has the same words ('its cone, its blind side').

edits.before: Loop this camera for two minutes. The Tech can leave the cabinet.
edits.after: Loop all three lenses for two minutes. The Tech can leave the cabinet.
edits.why: One loop takes the whole camera (CameraWatching: the loop is per camera), so the player knows the café, the terrace and the square all go quiet together.

edits.before: Cut this camera for good. The desk soon sees a dead screen.
edits.after: Cut the line to all three lenses for good. The desk soon sees a dead screen.
edits.why: One cut darkens all three (CameraDark). The Tech cuts its line at the cabinet. 'a dead screen' stays: it is the plate the player then sees (why.onWay.ways.screen, 'Dead screen · desk in {s} s').

The check below: the case Sky's loitering card will meet under B is route A's Fixer waiting beside Inez, and its {where} is this place. No courtyard is drawn there. It is the middle of the café terrace, between the café door (x -10.3) and the terrace wall's gate (x -4.3). The HUD calls it 'the café terrace' (the hint 'Watch the [café terrace]') and the people 'the terrace'. 'courtyard' was the mission file's name for the destination. It now shares its words with d:Under parasol, as both sides of the café share 'beside the café'. The hover reads: 'The mast camera saw the Fixer hanging about on the café terrace.'

edits.before: The mast camera covers the square. · It turns between three views. I've got the square. · The mast turns. The square's all it watches.
edits.after: The mast camera covers the café, the terrace and the square. · Three lenses up there, and none of them moves. · It watches the café and the square, all three ways at once.
edits.why: Silent in play since brief 102, but its lines stay so one moment can come back. They were untrue (it turns). No `hand` mark: a silent row is no item of any writer run.

edits.before: Mast camera. Three views, one lens. · It pans the square. I have the turns. · One lens on a slow pan. I know its views.
edits.after: Mast camera. Three fixed lenses, all live. · Café, terrace and square. No pan on any of them. · Three lenses, no pan. I know what each one covers.
edits.why: As the Scout's row: one panning lens was untrue. Written to match the other cameras' Tech rows ('No pan, no zoom.').
